lines.cap: **Narrator:** This is Kavya. She is twelve. Deepavali morning, a flat in Block 208.
**Kavya:** My maths test came back. Factorise **12x + 18**. I wrote **12(x + 18)**.
**Dad:** Looks fine to me. Same numbers, same letters. **Same thing.**
**Kavya:** Mr Tan wrote **REVISE**. In red. **Retest on Monday.**
**Mum:** No revising today. **Fifty guests** at four! Kavya: goodie bags. Ah Boy: don't touch the ladoos.
**Ah Boy:** I haven't touched any ladoos.
**Narrator:** But this documentary is about the **x** on her test.
**Agent X:** The name's **X**. Just X. My value is **classified**.
**Agent X:** Today I'm **5**. Tomorrow, **−3**. I could be anyone.
**Agent X:** Her answer? Expand it: **12x + 216**. Cover. Blown.
**Agent X:** Mission: get Kavya through Monday's retest. Without fifty guests noticing.
**Ah Boy:** Mum! There's a **spy** in Kavya's homework!
**Mum:** Then he can help with the goodie bags.
**Narrator:** On Good Terms. Episode 9: The Open House.
**Narrator:** One p.m. Dad is in charge of the **fairy lights**.
**Dad:** The window is a **square**, side **s**. Lights go all the way round: **P = 4s**.
**Agent X:** A **formula**. The letters are real quantities: **perimeter** and **side**.
**Dad:** Side **1.2 m**, so P = **4.8 m**. I've got **5**. Engineer.
**Ah Boy:** I've got **4** bags of sweets, the same in each, and **3** loose: **4x + 3**!
**Agent X:** An **expression**. No equals sign. I could be **any** number. My favourite job.
**Ah Boy:** I counted. **23**! So **4x + 3 = 23**.
**Agent X:** An **equation**. Now I'm one **particular** number: **5**. I hate equations.
**Kavya:** Put **3** more in **every** bag: **4(x + 3)**. That's always **4x + 12**.
**Agent X:** An **identity**: **4(x + 3) ≡ 4x + 12**. True for **every** x.
**Dad:** Easy. **4(x + 2) = 4x + 2**. Same thing.
**Agent X:** Undercover as **0**: **8** on the left, **2** on the right. One **counter-example**. Cover. Blown.
**Kavya:** My test: **5x² − 3x + 7**. Three **terms**. The sign in front **belongs** to the term.
**Agent X:** **Coefficients**: **5** and **−3**. The **7** has no letter: the **constant**.
**Ah Boy:** And the coefficient of just **x**?
**Agent X:** **1.** It's invisible. Like me.
**Narrator:** Two p.m. Priya brings **rangoli tiles**.
**Priya:** Priya. Best friend. Big tiles: **x by x**. Long tiles: **x by 1**.
**Square:** **x squared**, darling. An **area**. Don't confuse me with the help.
**Stick:** Stick. I'm **x**. A length. Chill.
**Dad:** **3x² + 2x − x²**. Add the lot: **4x³**!
**Agent X:** Undercover as **10**. The start is **220**. Dad's answer is **4000**. Cover blown.
**Square:** Only **like terms** combine: the **same letters** with the **same powers**.
**Priya:** Squares: **3x² − x² = 2x²**. Plus **2x**. Check: **220**.
**Square:** **x + x = 2x**: a length. But **x × x** makes **me**: **x²**. An **area**.
**Priya:** So **3x × 2x = 6x²**: six squares. Numbers times numbers, letters times letters.
**Agent X:** **Index laws.** Multiplying: **add** the powers. **x⁴ × x³ = x⁷**.
**Priya:** So **x³ × x⁴ = x¹²**!
**Square:** **x⁷**, darling. Multiply only for a **power of a power**: **(x³)⁴ = x¹²**.
**Agent X:** Dividing: **subtract** the powers. **y⁶ ÷ y² = y⁴**. And **x⁰ = 1**.
**Ah Boy:** I made a rangoli out of **ladoos**. ...It's gone now.
**Narrator:** Half past two. Revision. Ah Boy has the calculator.
**Kavya:** Find **x²** when **x = −3**.
**Ah Boy:** Easy! Minus 3, squared: **−9**!
**Agent X:** Undercover as **−3**. My disguise: **brackets**. Without them, my minus sign falls off.
**Agent X:** **(−3)² = 9**. Type −3² and the calculator squares only the **3**.
**Kavya:** So **bracket every value**. Then **BIDMAS**.
**Ah Boy:** My turn! x = 5, so **3x** is **35**!
**Agent X:** **3x** means **3 × x**: **15**. I'm a number, not a digit.
**Kavya:** And **2x²** at x = 3: square **first**. 2 × 9 = **18**, not 36.
**Uncle Ravi:** Kavya! Happy Deepavali from **Miami**! Kulfi freezes at **−15 °C**. My freezer only speaks **Fahrenheit**!
**Uncle Ravi:** Five degrees? In Miami that's an emergency.
**Agent X:** Fractions too. x = **½**: **8x² = 8 × ¼ = 2**.
**Ah Boy:** Can you go undercover as a ladoo?
**Agent X:** ...I could be anyone.
**Narrator:** Four p.m. Guests arrive in **families**.
**Mum:** Greet **everyone** in the family. Not just the first one.
**Handy:** Handy! The term **outside the bracket**. **Everyone inside gets a handshake!**
**Ah Boy:** **3(x + 4)**! I shook hands with x: **3x + 4**!
**Kavya:** Like an area: **4** by **x + 3** is **4x** plus **12**. Our identity!
**Handy:** A **negative** outside **flips every sign**: **−2(3x − 5) = −6x + 10**.
**Agent X:** Undercover as **0**: **8** and **−8**. Cover blown. −2 × −4 = **+8**.
**Mr Tan:** Mr Tan. Happy Deepavali. **Letters** work too: **x(x + 3) = x² + 3x**.
**Mr Tan:** Expand and simplify **3(2x + 1) − 2(x − 4)**.
**Mr Tan:** Why did the bracket come to the open house? To **expand** its social circle.
**Narrator:** Five p.m. Goodie bags. Kavya's least favourite word: **factorising**.
**Mum:** **12** packets of murukku, **18** ladoos. Every bag **identical**. As many as possible.
**Kavya:** Murukku in a packet? Nobody knows. Call it **x**. That's **12x + 18**.
**Ah Boy:** **Three** bags! **3(4x + 6)**!
**Agent X:** Both expand back to 12x + 18. But **6x + 9** still splits by **3**. Not **fully** factorised.
**Kavya:** Most bags: the **highest common factor** of 12 and 18. **6** bags, each with **2** packets and **3** ladoos.
**Agent X:** **12x + 18 = 6(2x + 3)**. Expand to check. **Identity confirmed.**
**Mr Tan:** Now the **hardest** one on Monday's retest: **6x²y + 9xy²**.
**Agent X:** Then we pull a heist. **The Great Factor Heist.** We take out **everything every term has**.
**Agent X:** The line-up. **6x²y = 2 × 3 × x × x × y**. **9xy² = 3 × 3 × x × y × y**.
**Priya:** Both terms have a **3**.
**Kavya:** **Two** x's in the first, only **one** in the second. Take **one x**: the **lowest power**.
**Priya:** And **one y**. The HCF is **3xy**!
**Agent X:** **3xy** goes outside. Inside: what's left. **2x** and **3y**.
**Kavya:** **6x²y + 9xy² = 3xy(2x + 3y)**!
**Agent X:** Put it all back: **3xy × 2x = 6x²y**, **3xy × 3y = 9xy²**. **Identity confirmed.**
**Agent X:** **5 ÷ 5 = 1**. So **5(x + 1)**. Never leave anyone behind.
**Kavya:** I think I actually **like** factorising.
**Ah Boy:** Also, there are only **17** ladoos.
**Agent X:** 12 and 17 share no factor but **1**. **One** goodie bag.
**Narrator:** Six p.m. Ah Boy performs **magic**.
**Ah Boy:** Think of a number. **Double** it. **Add 10**. Cut it in **half**. Take away your number.
**Ah Boy:** Your answer is... **5**!
**Mr Tan:** Five. Remarkable.
**Agent X:** Call it **n**. Double: **2n**. Add 10. Half of that: **n + 5**. Take away n: **5**.
**Kavya:** **5** for **every** n. It's an **identity**!
**Priya:** My trick: '**n less than 10**'. That's **n − 10**.
**Agent X:** It **starts** at 10: **10 − n**. '10 less than n' is **n − 10**.
**Dad:** '**Add 3, then double**': **2n + 3**. Same thing.
**Agent X:** Undercover as **4**: **14**. But 2n + 3 gives **11**. Cover blown. **2(n + 3)**.
**Priya:** I had **p** dollars. I spent **a quarter** on a gift and **$3** on bubble tea. Left: **¾p − 3**.
**Mum:** Taxis! **$4** flag-down, plus **70 cents** a kilometre. **5 km**: **$7.50**.
**Kavya:** **12 km**: **$12.40**. Only the distance changes: **C = 4 + 0.7d**.
**Agent X:** A **formula**. **C** is the **subject**: the letter on its own.
**Narrator:** Nine p.m. Uncle Ravi calls again.
**Uncle Ravi:** Kavya! It's **77 °F** here. What's that in **Celsius**?
**Phil:** Phil. **Function machine.** Celsius in. **× 9/5**, **+ 32**. Fahrenheit out.
**Kavya:** Run it **backwards**, in **reverse order**. 77 **− 32** = 45. **× 5/9**: **25 °C**.
**Ah Boy:** Like **socks and shoes**! Socks go on first, so they come off **last**.
**Ah Boy:** ...Can someone help me with my socks?
**Phil:** **Changing the subject**: **F − 32 = 9/5 C**, so **C = 5/9 (F − 32)**.
**Agent X:** Now **C** is on its own. Lucky C.
**Agent X:** Undercover as **2**: y = **12**. Dad's formula gives **−2**. Cover blown.
**Phil:** Shoes off first: **− 6**, then **÷ 3**. **x = (y − 6)/3**.
**Handy:** **Double** brackets! Everyone in one shakes hands with everyone in the other. **Four** handshakes!
**Dad:** So **(x + 4)² = x² + 16**. Same thing.
**Agent X:** You missed two **4x** handshakes: **x² + 8x + 16**. Cover blown.

chapters.title: The open house saves you some marks

lines.cap: **Narrator:** Before the credits: six ways to save marks.
**Dad:** One. **Unlike terms** don't combine: **2a + 3b** is not 5ab. Not the same thing.
**Handy:** Two. Everyone inside gets a handshake: **3(x + 4) = 3x + 12**.
**Mum:** Three. A negative flips **both** signs: **−3(x − 2) = −3x + 6**.
**Ah Boy:** Four. Bracket your negatives: if x = −5, **x² = 25**. I gave the calculator back.
**Square:** Five. **2x²** at x = 3 is **18**, not 36. Square first, darling.
**Kavya:** Six. Factorise **fully**, and never lose a term: **5x + 5 = 5(x + 1)**.
**Narrator:** On Good Terms will return.
**Mr Tan:** Monday. Kavya, your retest. Factorising: **ten out of ten**.
**Ah Boy:** Agent X! Think of a number. Double it, add 10, cut it in half, take away your number.
**Ah Boy:** Your answer is **5**!
**Agent X:** ...How did you know?
